newsitem.title: UK: Centrica sees no contract renegotiations yet.
newsitem.headline: Centrica sees no contract renegotiations yet.

text.p: Centrica Plc, recently demerged from British Gas, does not expect to renegotiate any more long term take-or-pay contracts for some time yet, chief executive Roy Gardner told a news conference on Thursday.
"After the BP and Mobil deals there was a lot of interest from other companies looking to reach a deal, but there's nothing imminent," said Gardner.
In the fourth quarter of last year British Gas Plc, concluded three contract renegotiations with British Petroleum Co Plc, Mobil Corp, and British Gas' own Exploration and Production business.
"We're continuing to talk to all major producers," he said, adding that a satisfactory position will not be reached until the end of the year.

Following last year's renegotiations, Centrica reduced its obligations to buy gas by 11.3 billion therms, mostly over the next five years, and cut the contract price to market-related levels on a further 15 billion therms to be phased in over a number of years.
An exceptional charge of 341 million stg was made to cover these deals, chairman Richard Giordano said in a statement to accompany British Gas' full year results for 1996 on Thursday.
Earlier this month, British Gas demerged its gas supply business into a new company, Centrica, and changed the name of its remaining gas transport and storage business to BG Plc.
